findings.title: Include the identity type in denial-cache keys
findings.body: The denial key uses only the parsed UserUID, so distinct subjects such as `anonymous:0` and `render:0` share an entry for the same action, resource name, and folder. If an anonymous dashboard-read check is denied, a subsequent renderer check hits that denial before reaching the renderer's unconditional read grant. This incorrectly blocks rendering for 30 seconds. Include the identity type or full typed subject in the key.

findings.title: Encode denial-cache key components unambiguously
findings.body: Joining the resource name and parent folder with underscores creates collisions for UIDs containing underscores. For example, `(name="a_b", parent="c")` and `(name="a", parent="b_c")` produce the same key for the same user and action. Denying the first request therefore also denies the second, even if its permissions allow access, because denial-cache hits bypass permission evaluation. Use an escaped, length-prefixed, or structured encoding of the components.

findings.title: Use an actual cached grant in the denial-precedence test
findings.body: The test says it grants dashboard access to prove that the denial entry takes precedence, but the cached scope value is `false`, which `checkPermission` treats as no grant. The fake permission store also returns no permissions, so the test still passes if the denial-cache lookup is removed entirely. Set this scope to `true` so the test detects failure to honor the denial entry.
